q: The Collatz graph G = (ℕ, →) where n → Syr(n) is a directed graph. The Collatz conjecture states that G has a specific tree structure. Specifically:
opts: G is a tree rooted at 1
G has a unique infinite connected component but may have multiple fixed points
G is a forest with one root per cycle
G would be a tree rooted at 1 iff the conjecture holds — every positive integer eventually maps to 1
exp: If the Collatz conjecture holds, every positive integer eventually reaches 1, making G a directed tree rooted at 1 (every node has exactly one outgoing edge, and all paths lead to 1). The conjecture fails iff some orbit never reaches 1 — either diverging or cycling at a different value.
